Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree so you don't collide with parallel work happening on this same repo right now:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-roles -b feature/freemc-roles main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-roles`, symlink node_modules from the primary tree if it's not already usable (`ls node_modules` — if missing/broken: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`), and symlink the env: `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env` if `.env` isn't present. Do ALL your work in this worktree, not in /opt/nxeon directly.

This worktree already has a 12-mode "free Minecraft server" product on main (commit c2e97e9): one free Docker-based Minecraft server per account on a dedicated VM ("freemc-host", a real `Server` row with `hostname="freemc-host"`), managed via RCON. Every `kind:"plugins"` preset in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`'s `FREEMC_PRESETS` now bundles the LuckPerms permissions plugin (this was just added platform-wide specifically so a roles feature would work everywhere plugins run) — `kind:"properties"` presets (Vanilla/Creative/Hardcore/Peaceful) do NOT have LuckPerms, since they run no plugins at all.

READ FIRST, in full: `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` and `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`. Key patterns:
- `sendRcon(host, containerName, userId, command)` in free-minecraft-control.ts — the existing helper for `docker exec <container> rcon-cli <cmd>` over SSH. Reuse it.
- `getFreeMinecraftPlayers`/`getFreeServerPlayers` — online-players helper.
- `shellQuote` (from `lib/ssh-exec.ts`) — every value interpolated into a remote command must go through validation/escaping. For this feature specifically: role names and permission nodes must come from fixed allowlists you define, never raw free text passed straight into an RCON command — a role name or "custom command" field is effectively code running on shared infrastructure if not constrained.
- `withServerSsh(host, async (conn) => {...})` + `exec(conn, cmd, timeoutMs)` — get the host via `db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`.
- `FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION = "26.1.2"` — pin this VERSION on any plugins-kind test container you boot.

YOUR TASK — build a roles & command-permissions feature backed by LuckPerms via RCON. No new DB schema/migration: LuckPerms owns all the role/permission state itself inside the container (in its own H2 database), so nothing needs to persist in our Postgres — every read is a live RCON query.

1. Research and LIVE-VERIFY the exact LuckPerms console command syntax (do not trust memory/training data — LuckPerms syntax has had minor changes across versions, and you must confirm against the actual bundled version, which was v5.5.71 as of this session but re-check). Boot a real test container on freemc-host (container name `mc-rolestest`, use a `kind:"plugins"` preset as your base — e.g. adapt `FREEMC_PRESETS.towny`'s env, or any plugins preset — VERSION=26.1.2, ENABLE_RCON=true, reasonable memory), then via `docker exec mc-rolestest rcon-cli "<cmd>"` confirm:
   - Creating a group: `/lp creategroup <name>`
   - Listing groups: `/lp listgroups`
   - Granting a permission node to a group: `/lp group <name> permission set <node> true` (and `false`/unset for revoking)
   - Assigning a player to a group: `/lp user <player> parent add <group>` (confirm this works by username alone, without the player needing to be online — this matters since role assignment shouldn't require someone to be actively connected)
   - Deleting a group: `/lp deletegroup <name>`
   Also investigate what's actually reliable for gating COMMANDS specifically (not just abstract permission nodes): EssentialsX commands are gated by `essentials.command.<cmd>` nodes (confirm a couple, e.g. `essentials.command.give`, `essentials.command.tp`), and note that gating raw VANILLA commands (not backed by a plugin) via LuckPerms has real limitations — Paper only checks permissions for commands that are actually permission-gated by a plugin or Paper itself; something like `/gamemode` IS permission-gated by Paper itself (`minecraft.command.gamemode`) so should work. Build your curated command list from commands you've CONFIRMED are permission-gated (test a couple of denials live: create a restricted group, don't grant a node, and confirm the actual behavior is "permission denied" rather than silently still working) rather than assuming. Report honestly if some command you expected to be gate-able turns out not to work reliably — don't ship a control that silently does nothing.
   Clean up your test container/data dir and any throwaway scripts before finishing.

2. Build `lib/freemc-command-catalog.ts` — exports a curated `FREEMC_GATEABLE_COMMANDS: { node: string; label: string; plugin: string }[]` — only commands/nodes you've actually confirmed work, spanning the commonly-bundled plugins (EssentialsX commands, a few core Paper/vanilla ones you confirmed are gate-able, plugin-specific ones like Towny/Prison commands where relevant since those presets are common). Doesn't need to be exhaustive — a solid confirmed set of 15-25 is fine.

3. Build `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts` — `"use server"`, actions for: create role, delete role, toggle a command-node permission on a role (on/off, validated against `FREEMC_GATEABLE_COMMANDS`), assign a player to a role, remove a player from a role, list current roles + their granted nodes + their members (all via live RCON queries — `/lp listgroups`, `/lp group <name> info`/`permission info`, `/lp group <name> listmembers` or equivalent — confirm the actual output-parsing approach works against real RCON responses, which can be plain text you'll need to parse reasonably, not JSON). `requireUser()` + ownership check + `checkRateLimit` (reuse from `lib/rate-limit.ts`, same pattern as other actions in `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`) on every mutating action. Every action must first check the caller's server's active preset has `kind === "plugins"` (via `FREEMC_PRESETS[row.preset]`) and return a clear error otherwise — no LuckPerms means no roles feature.

4. Build `components/customer/freemc/RolesTab.tsx` — `"use client"`. Shows a clear "Available on plugin-based game modes only" message when the active preset is `kind:"properties"`. Otherwise: role list with create/delete, per-role a checklist of `FREEMC_GATEABLE_COMMANDS` to toggle, and a player-assignment section (text input for player name — validate as a plausible Minecraft username shape, e.g. `/^[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,16}$/` — plus a role picker). Match the existing Tailwind visual style in `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` (`card`, `btn-primary`, `input` utility classes, dark navy theme — read that file for exact conventions).

5. Do NOT edit `FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, `actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, or any other existing file — only create the new files above. Do NOT merge to main or push anywhere. Do NOT delete your worktree when done — I'll integrate from it and clean it up myself.

6. Before finishing: `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` in your worktree must both pass clean. Commit your work in the worktree (git add the new files explicitly, never `git add -A`) so it's not lost.

Report back: the exact LuckPerms command syntax you verified (paste real command/response pairs from your live testing), the final gateable-command catalog, any limitation you found (especially around vanilla-command gating) stated plainly, the file paths created, the worktree path/branch name, and confirmation the build/typecheck passed.

1	/**
2	 * Docker/RCON control primitives for free-tier Minecraft containers on
3	 * freemc-host — the free-tier equivalent of lib/game-control.ts, which speaks
4	 * to full Proxmox-VM game servers over SSH+tunnelled RCON. This is much
5	 * simpler: one SSH hop to the host, then `docker exec <container> ...` for
6	 * everything, using the CLI tools itzg/docker-minecraft-server already bundles
7	 * (rcon-cli, mc-monitor) instead of a hand-rolled RCON protocol client.
8	 *
9	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from both lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
10	 * and, in future, a worker sweep, same reasoning as lib/game-control.ts.
11	 */
12	import { scryptSync } from "node:crypto";
13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
15	
16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}
28	
29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}
33	
34	export type ServerStatus = {
35	  running: boolean;
36	  players: { online: number; max: number } | null;
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
52	    return { running: false, players: null };
53	  }
54	  const status = await dockerExec(
55	    conn,
56	    containerName,
57	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
58	    10_000,
59	  );
60	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
61	  try {
62	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);

## Summary

**Worktree:** `/opt/nxeon-wt-roles`, branch `feature/freemc-roles`, commit `2e39311` (not pushed, not merged, not deleted).

**Files created:**
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-roles/lib/freemc-command-catalog.ts` — `FREEMC_GATEABLE_COMMANDS` (18 EssentialsX + 6 Paper/vanilla nodes)
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-roles/lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts` — server actions (create/delete role, toggle permission, assign/remove player, list roles)
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-roles/components/customer/freemc/RolesTab.tsx` — client UI

**`npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` both pass clean (exit 0, no errors/warnings).**

### Live LuckPerms testing — the key finding

Booted a real `mc-rolestest` container (Paper 26.1.2, LuckPerms v5.5.71, from the Towny plugins preset) and discovered the RCON text-response channel for `/lp ...` commands is **completely broken**: every LuckPerms command (`creategroup`, `permission set`, `parent add`, `listgroups`, etc.) returns an empty RCON response, always — verified across both H2 and yaml storage, and with the RCON connection deliberately held open 4s+ past the command. The commands *do* execute (confirmed by reading LuckPerms' own storage back afterward — e.g. `lp creategroup vip` → `stdout=""` but `vip.yml` appeared with `name: vip`), but LuckPerms dispatches command handling on its own async thread pool and whatever it sends back never reaches the RCON socket (Bukkit's RCON feedback collector is already torn down by the time it arrives) — and it isn't logged to console either, so it's simply discarded. Sync commands on the same container (vanilla `list`/`seed`, Paper's `/plugins`) return real text fine, confirming this is LP-specific, not a general RCON problem.

**Consequence for the design:** mutations still go over RCON (fire-and-forget), but every *read* — listing roles, their permissions, their members — parses LuckPerms' own `yaml-storage/groups/*.yml` and `yaml-storage/users/*.yml` files directly via SSH `cat`, not RCON text. This required switching LP's storage from its H2 default to `yaml` (H2 isn't parseable without a JDBC driver), applied idempotently and lazily by `ensureLuckPermsReady()` in the new actions file.

**Second finding:** LuckPerms' default `use-server-uuid-cache: false` makes `/lp user <name> parent add <group>` silently no-op for a player who has never joined — no user file is ever created. Flipping that config key (bundled into the same bootstrap) fixed it; verified the created user file's UUID matched Node's own offline-UUID computation (`MD5("OfflinePlayer:"+name)`, patched to v3) byte-for-byte, so role assignment now works by username alone as required.

**Third finding (catalog correction):** the task's assumed EssentialsX convention `essentials.command.<cmd>` is wrong — extracting `EssentialsX-2.22.0.jar`'s plugin.yml and in-jar string constants showed the real convention is `essentials.<cmd>` (e.g. `essentials.give`, `essentials.heal`), with one irregular case: `/tp`'s node is `essentials.teleport`, not `essentials.tp`.

**Honest limitation:** true in-game "deny" testing (grant nothing, confirm the command fails) could not be done — RCON always runs as a permission-bypassing console sender by Bukkit design (so no RCON-issued command can ever be observed being denied, regardless of LuckPerms state), and no real Minecraft client library supports this environment's protocol version to connect a bot. This is documented plainly in both new files' header comments rather than papered over.

Test container `mc-rolestest` and its data directory (`/opt/freemc/servers/rolestest`) on freemc-host were fully removed; all throwaway scripts were deleted before committing.
